subject: Post-demo: cost & batching assumptions for VectorStor POC
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Joe Taylor <joe.taylor@vectorstor.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: cost & batching assumptions for VectorStor POC

Thanks again for taking the demo today, Joe — good conversation. Quick recap and the few items we need from you to size a realistic PoC/estimate on cost and expected latency with continuous batching enabled.

Recap of what we heard (please correct if I mis-stated):
- Primary workload: real-time vector search + short completion edits for results enrichment.
- Target audience: end-user search UX with spikes during business hours and heavy tail on marketing campaigns.
- Preferred model family: open Llama-variant (24B) for quality/cost tradeoff.

What we need from you to firm up numbers (attached a short PoC estimator template):
1) Typical request size (prompt + expected completion) in tokens and p50/p90 sizes
2) Expected token volume for pilot (2 wks) and first 3 months (tokens/month)
3) Peak concurrency (sustained vs burst) and average RPS windows (1m/5m)
4) Percentage of calls that are streamed (server-sent tokens) vs non-streaming
5) Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p90 p95) or per-user SLOs we should target

Notes on batching assumptions:
- Our hosted runtime supports continuous batching (requests pooled across connections) to reduce unit cost. That usually helps when per-request tokens are small/medium and concurrency is moderate.
- Continuous batching has trade-offs vs strict per-request latency: we can tune target batching windows and max batch size if you need tighter tail latency.

Request: please attach a simple traffic sample (CSV or CSV-like) and rough budget target — i.e., target $/1M tokens you want us to hit for a production contract. That helps us propose specific cost scenarios.

Attachments: redwood_poc_estimator_template.xlsx (xlsx)

Next steps: if you can send the items above by EOD Thu (Oct 8) we can return a 2-scenario estimate (pilot + production) and a proposed PoC kickoff plan. Proposing a 30-min follow-up later this week to go over numbers (I pasted some available slots below).

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Joe Taylor <joe.taylor@vectorstor.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost & batching assumptions for VectorStor POC

Camila — great demo, thanks. See answers below and attached a small sample traffic export. Happy to walk through details on a call.

Answers to your list:
1) Typical request size: 1,800 tokens average (prompt ~300 tokens; completion avg ~1,500), p50 1,200, p90 3,400
2) Token volumes:
   - Pilot (2 weeks): ~12M tokens total (~850k/day during pilot weekdays)
   - Q1 expected (post-pilot ramp): 100M tokens/month
3) Concurrency:
   - Sustained peak: ~80 concurrent requests
   - Burst: up to ~350 concurrent lasting 10–20 minutes during marketing pushes
   - Baseline outside peak: ~8–12 concurrent
4) Streaming vs non-streaming: ~70% of calls will stream (UI shows progressive results), 30% are non-streaming batch edits
5) Latency SLOs: p50 <250ms, p90 <600ms for the interactive search flow (we can tolerate slightly higher p95 in bursts if explained)

Budget target: our procurement target is about $750 per 1M tokens for initial production pricing. Pilot can be higher (we understand PoCs carry overhead) but we want to see a path toward that target in the production proposal.

Attachment: vectorstor_token_profile.csv (csv) — includes timestamped request sizes, streaming flag, and session IDs for ~3 days of traffic.

Let me know if you want any other slices (user vs system traffic). We prefer the kickoff next week if you can get a proposal ready.

—Joe
Joe Taylor
Head of Product | VectorStor
joe.taylor@vectorstor.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost & batching assumptions for VectorStor POC

Thanks Joe — this is very helpful and gives us a good starting point. I reviewed the sample and sketched two cost scenarios (attached):
- Scenario A (Pilot-focused): conservative concurrency assumptions, higher per-token during onboarding.
- Scenario B (Production ramp): assumes continuous batching tuned to your traffic profile and 30% lower per-token unit cost vs A once warmed and autoscaled.

I attached an initial estimate (redwood_cost_estimate.xlsx) and a short PoC plan:
- Week 0: kickoff, collection of final traffic slices and credentials (read-only)
- Week 1: ingest traffic, configure batching windows & cache rules, run controlled load tests
- Week 2: monitor live pilot, optimize batching/quantization knobs, produce final run-rate estimate

POC success metrics (suggested):
- Achieve production-like throughput while meeting p50/p90 latency targets above
- Demonstrate >20% end-to-end cost reduction from baseline by enabling continuous batching and prefix caching
- Show stable autoscale behavior across 10x normal -> burst windows

Questions for you:
- Is $750/1M tokens an inflexible target for procurement, or is there a band (ex: $600–$900) that would get internal approval?
- Can you share whether session affinity matters (i.e., can we route requests across workers for batching) or does your application require strict single-connection locality?

Attached: redwood_cost_estimate.xlsx (xlsx)

Proposed times for quick 30-min follow-up: Thu Oct 8 10:00–10:30 PT, Thu Oct 8 15:00–15:30 PT, Fri Oct 9 09:00–09:30 PT. Please confirm and we’ll send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Camila

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Joe Taylor <joe.taylor@vectorstor.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost & batching assumptions for VectorStor POC

Adding a couple technical notes on continuous batching and what I’d recommend we instrument during the pilot: 

1) Continuous batching expectations
- For your token sizes (p50 ~1,200, p90 ~3,400) continuous batching will still help because we can batch partially completed streams and pad smaller requests into larger kernels. Expect the biggest gains when there are many concurrent small/medium requests (i.e., your baseline + mid peaks).
- Target window: start with 10–20ms batching target, max batch size 64; we can relax to 40–60ms if you need lower p95.

2) Concurrency and shard sizing
- Based on your bursts (up to 350): recommend per-shard concurrency cap of ~200; plan for 2 shards for headroom + autoscale buffers. That keeps tail latency predictable while allowing us to reach high throughput.

3) Cache & KV warmup
- Prefix/KV cache warms will materially reduce tokens served for repeated user flows. Capture top-100 prefixes during Week 1 load test and confirm cache-hit rate.

4) Metrics to capture (we’ll produce dashboards):
- tokens/sec, tokens/req, batch size distribution, batch wait time, p50/p90/p95 latency, cache hit ratio, per-shard CPU/GPU utilization

I’ll include example autoscale settings and a sample k8s/VM plan in the kickoff doc. Happy to jump on the call for a quick tech sync to validate shard counts.

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
